items.title: Smooth positive approximation of a measurable time coefficient

source.anchor: Original Samplinglib finite-interval approximation supplement. Smooth positive approximation of a measurable time coefficient.
source.attribution: Original Samplinglib supplement. The linked Mathlib source is analytic background.

items.statement: For every measurable coefficient with the stated almost-everywhere range on \([a,b]\), there is a globally smooth real function \(g\) that is strictly positive and at most \(C+\varepsilon\) at every point of that interval, and whose integrated absolute error is less than \(\varepsilon\).
assumptions: The endpoints \(a,b\) are real with \(a\le b\). All integrals are Lebesgue integrals restricted to the closed interval \([a,b]\). The case \(a=b\) is included.
The constants satisfy \(C\ge0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\). The function \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is Borel measurable.
The range condition \(0\le f(t)\le C\) holds almost everywhere on \([a,b]\). No condition is placed on its values outside that interval or on its exceptional null set.

formulae.label: Claim
formulae.tex: \exists g\in C^\infty(\mathbb R),\quad 0<g(t)\le C+\varepsilon\ (a\le t\le b),\qquad \int_a^b |g(t)-f(t)|\,dt<\varepsilon.

obligations.label: Smooth positive approximation of a measurable time coefficient

bindings.boundary: The approximation is for one prescribed finite interval and tolerance. Smoothness holds on all of \(\mathbb R\); positivity and the displayed upper bound are guaranteed on \([a,b]\). This result controls coefficient integrals. Convergence of solutions and passage of density estimates to limits require further arguments.

assumption_deltas.source: The endpoints \(a,b\) are real with \(a\le b\). All integrals are Lebesgue integrals restricted to the closed interval \([a,b]\). The case \(a=b\) is included.
assumption_deltas.lean: Real ordered endpoints, volume restricted to Icc a b.
assumption_deltas.reason: An interval of zero length is included and has zero integral.

assumption_deltas.source: The constants satisfy \(C\ge0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\). The function \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is Borel measurable.
assumption_deltas.lean: Nonnegative C, strictly positive epsilon, and Measurable f on the real Borel space.
assumption_deltas.reason: Integrability follows inside the proof from the finite interval and essential bound.

assumption_deltas.source: The range condition \(0\le f(t)\le C\) holds almost everywhere on \([a,b]\). No condition is placed on its values outside that interval or on its exceptional null set.
assumption_deltas.lean: The restricted-volume almost-everywhere range of f is Icc 0 C.
assumption_deltas.reason: All estimates on f are almost everywhere. The constructed g is globally smooth and has pointwise range bounds on the chosen interval.

items.title: One approximation for a coefficient and its noise amplitude

source.anchor: Original Samplinglib finite-interval approximation supplement. One approximation for a coefficient and its noise amplitude.
source.attribution: Original Samplinglib supplement. The linked Mathlib source is analytic background.

items.statement: Under the same assumptions there is one globally smooth function \(g\), positive and at most \(C+\varepsilon\) on \([a,b]\), for which both the integrated coefficient error and the integrated squared error of the noise amplitude \(\sqrt{2f}\) are less than \(\varepsilon\).
assumptions: The endpoints \(a,b\) are real with \(a\le b\). All integrals are Lebesgue integrals restricted to the closed interval \([a,b]\). The case \(a=b\) is included.
The constants satisfy \(C\ge0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\). The function \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is Borel measurable.
The range condition \(0\le f(t)\le C\) holds almost everywhere on \([a,b]\). No condition is placed on its values outside that interval or on its exceptional null set.

In the noise integral, Lean uses the total real square root, which is zero at negative inputs. Equivalently, replace \(f\) by a measurable nonnegative function agreeing with it almost everywhere on \([a,b]\). Its values on the exceptional null set do not affect this integral.
